title: Folder tree validator silently truncated large folder trees
answers: Why does folder tree migration validation report false differences on large folder trees?
Folder validator says folders differ between legacy and unified storage but they look the same
Unified storage migration validation false positive on many folders
body:
Symptom: FolderTreeValidator reported spurious folder-tree mismatches between legacy tables and unified storage on namespaces with many folders.
Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/migrations/validator.go buildUnifiedFolderParentMap issued a single Search request with a fixed Limit (100000), silently discarding folders beyond that limit.
Fix pattern: replace the single large-limit request with bounded pages, continuing from the SearchAfter cursor built from the last row's sort fields (row.GetSortFields()), looping until a page returns fewer than the page size.
Constraints: applies to any resourcepb Search consumer that needs the complete result set rather than a top-N sample; do not paginate with an offset for this API since concurrent creates/deletes shift offsets and can hide or duplicate rows.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/migrations code that queries resourcepb Search for a full result set
